justification: Changes the query the mounted assessment page sends for its DCP rule list. A wrong query serves rules for other land, or withholds rules that apply, so it is a served-answer change; but the route logic that decides is untouched (PR #1259) and only one new parameter is added.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The mounted component stops passing landFacts to the builder, or stops using the builder, or the builder drops or renames any parameter the page sent before. Forced: deleting the single landFacts line from ProvisionsByTocStructure.tsx turned the suite to 1 failed, 4 passed.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production route measured 2026-10-11 on 8 GLADSTONE STREET LILYFIELD via /api/provisions/for-property with former_council=inner_west (the page's fallback when the portal gives no former council): without land_facts meta.land_conditions = {withheld 0, unconfirmed 286}; with the portal's own landFacts = {withheld 214, unconfirmed 42}. On the 13 sampled Inner West addresses whose former council was known, the rule list was identical with and without land_facts (25,634 rules both ways).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With the landFacts line deleted from ProvisionsByTocStructure.tsx the run printed 'Tests: 1 failed, 4 passed, 5 total' (the mounted-component guard). Restored: 'Tests: 5 passed, 5 total'.

break_it.scenario: The portal returns no landFacts for a lot.
break_it.what_happens: The builder omits land_facts; the route keeps every site-specific rule as 'unconfirmed' and the page says it could not confirm the land -- the behaviour before this change, never a silent withhold.
break_it.how: encodeLandFacts(null) returns null and the param is not set; test 'omits land_facts when the portal gave none'.

break_it.scenario: The refactor silently changes a parameter the page already sent (heritage false dropped, hca renamed, land_application re-encoded).
break_it.what_happens: Every property's DCP list would change shape with no error -- the worst kind of regression.
break_it.how: Test 'keeps every parameter the page sent before' pins groupBy, former_council, zone, heritage=false, hca, precinct_id and land_application exactly as the inline code built them; heritage keeps the !== undefined check so false is still sent.

break_it.scenario: A future change wires the param into another unmounted hook again, as #1259 did.
break_it.what_happens: Tests pass while users see no change.
break_it.how: The guard reads the MOUNTED component's source and the assessment page's mount, not a hook; it fails if either stops holding.

mutation_analysis: Forced failure, not argued: removing the landFacts line from the component made the guard fail (1 failed, 4 passed); restoring it passed 5/5. A builder that returned an empty URLSearchParams would fail all three builder tests. A builder that always sent land_facts would fail the null-facts test.
residual_risk: The guard is a source-text regex: a rename of propertyData would fail it loudly (safe direction). The measured effect is on the inner_west fallback path only; how often real Inner West lots hit that fallback is not measured here -- 13 of 13 sampled lots had a former council. The served-answer audit (feat/served-answer-audit) measures what users see more broadly.

post_merge.manual_verify: Once deployed: open /assessment for 8 Gladstone Street Lilyfield and confirm the DCP request in the network tab carries land_facts.

pre_impl.existing_data: No table is written. The route already reads land_facts (decodeLandFacts + applyLandConditions in app/api/provisions/for-property/route.ts, PR #1259) and /api/property already returns constraints.landFacts; 292 live rows carry v2_land_condition, all source_council inner_west.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: PR #1259 assumed the page used hooks/useFullPropertyData.ts; nothing imports it. The mounted page is app/assessment/page.tsx -> ProvisionsByTocStructure, which built its own query. Also: on the usual path (former council known) these rules never reach the list at all; only the inner_west fallback serves them.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses encodeLandFacts and encodeLandApplication unchanged; the inline query moves into one pure builder so a test can see it. No route, schema or data change.

functions.name: buildForPropertyParams
functions.input: The page's former council, zone, heritage flag, conservation area name, precinct id, the portal's land application instruments and the portal's landFacts, each possibly missing.
functions.output: URLSearchParams for /api/provisions/for-property, identical to the previous inline query plus land_facts when the portal supplied facts.
functions.if_none: Missing inputs are simply not set; missing landFacts omits land_facts so the route keeps site rules as unconfirmed and says so on the page.
